detail.abstract: In July 2021, the ECB Governing Council committed to including climate change considerations in its monetary policy framework. This commitment involved, amongst other deliverables, new climate-related statistical indicators. The focus of this Article is on describing the new analytical indicators of carbon emissions for financial institutions resident in Ireland. The Irish values are broadly in line with the euro area responses although the headline statistics mask considerable heterogeneity. For some of the indicators, the highly globalised nature of the Irish economy makes it difficult to establish a link between the new analytical indicators of carbon emissions and the ongoing efforts of indigenous firms to transition towards a more carbon neutral production process. More disaggregated macroeconomic data in the coming years as input into the indicators combined with separate improvements planned to the estimation of these indicators will further assist policy makers in this regard.

detail.abstract: This Article introduces the experimental Distributional Wealth Accounts (DWA) for Ireland - a novel high-frequency dataset on household wealth consistent with National Accounts statistics, addressing increasing interest and growing demand for timely, consistent and internationally comparable information on the distribution of assets and liabilities across households. By linking Quarterly Sector Accounts with household survey data, DWA provide new insights on the growth of household wealth in Ireland on a quarterly basis. The data indicate that the overall increase in the net wealth of Irish households over the past decade has been accompanied by a significant reduction in inequality. This was mainly driven by strong growth in the net wealth of households in the bottom half of the distribution. Yet, the wealthiest 10 per cent of Irish households are more than five times as rich as those in the poorer half of the distribution altogether. One reason for this is the considerable heterogeneity in the composition of households’ balance sheets and the increasing concentration of housing assets amongst richer households. Over the past decade, while those in the bottom half of the net wealth distribution mainly benefited from a reduction of their liabilities, the richest 10 per cent of households witnessed an increase of their assets’ value.

title: Earnings Growth Under High Inflation

detail.title: Earnings Growth Under High Inflation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. QB3
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The Irish economy is currently experiencing a tight labour market and high inflation. Using the framework of the Phillips curve – which relates changes in wages to labour market tightness and inflation - we find that since 2018, nominal earnings growth has been lower than this model would predict. The gap between observed and estimated earnings growth based on the Phillips curve widened to 1.3 percentage points in 2022. Our analysis finds that this gap most likely reflects a delayed catch-up of wages to the sharp drop in real incomes in 2022. Fiscal supports and savings may also have contributed to dampening wage pressures by providing temporary cushioning to households. Our results suggest that a degree of real wage catch up is likely over the medium term. However, with the economy now operating at full capacity, it is important that the fiscal stance does not add further stimulus to the economy.

title: The Impact of the 2016 Finance Act on Investment into Irish Real Estate Funds

detail.title: The Impact of the 2016 Finance Act on Investment into Irish Real Estate Funds

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 2
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the impact that the 2016 Finance Act on investment into Irish real estate investment funds (IREFs). The Act introduced a 20% tax rate on the distributions and capital gains from IREF equity for most foreign investors. To understand the impact of this change, a novel investor-level dataset is analysed using difference-indifference and triple difference models. I find that the average investor whose tax status changed did not alter their investment behaviour, relative to investors whose tax status did not change. Investors who were the only investor in a fund (single investors) responded by reducing net subscriptions by 16.6-18.5 percentage points more than other investors who saw their tax status change. This corresponds to an elasticity of around-1. Estimating the regressions in an event study format, it becomes clear that single investors' reaction to the tax change was concentrated in Q4 2016, the period during which the tax was announced but before it came into effect. Consulting the financial statements of these funds, an explanation emerges-a substantial minority of single investor funds responded to the tax change by providing loans to fund dividends and redemptions. Constructing a series for shareholder lending from the financial statements, I am able to confirm this empirically. Therefore, the primary, but unintended, consequence of the 2016 IREF tax was the swapping of equity for shareholder loans by single investor funds, in an effort to reduce their tax liability resulting from the policy change.

detail.abstract: Urban green spaces are recognized as essential elements of cities. They offer multiple benefits, including mitigating the urban heat island effect and its negative impact on public health. They also present opportunities for people to interact, recreate, and connect with nature. Rapid urbanization leads to a significant transformation of green spaces to impervious surfaces and urban infrastructures. A large number of cities throughout the world have experienced "urban heat island" (UHI) effects. UHI are characterized by a temperature difference between urban and rural regions. Urban green spaces can contribute to a broad range of ecosystem services, among which temperature mitigation is regarded as an important ecosystem regulating service. Understanding the influences of green space dynamics on the temperature variability is therefore of great interest for mitigating the UHI effect in cities. The UHI effect can be assessed by measuring surface air temperature and land surface temperature in the system. This study investigated green space dynamics and land surface temperature in the Vijayawada City, Andhra Pradesh, India. This research study addresses the pressing concern of environmental stress and green infrastructure (GI) deficiency, a rapidly urbanizing Tier-II study city. The central empirical concern is to assess spatial patterns of ecological degradation by integrating satellite-derived indices viz., Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Urban Heat Island (UHI), Air Quality Index (AQI), and City Biodiversity Index (CBI). These indicators are employed to diagnose areas with inadequate green cover, extreme thermal exposure, and air quality, which often overlap with low-income and high-density urban zones.

detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and the measures put in place to control its spread have resulted in a collapse in economic activity around the world. The long-term recovery path from this deep economic shock is uncertain. In this article we explore different potential recovery scenarios over the medium term and the economic mechanisms that will influence the shape of the recovery. In the baseline scenario, output rebounds strongly but the recovery is incomplete by 2025, with output still below the level that could have been achieved had COVID-19 not occurred. A severe adverse scenario could see persistently high unemployment until the middle of the decade. Policy interventions by governments and central banks will play an important role in ensuring the economy recovers within a reasonable timeframe. We estimate that domestic and international policy responses announced to date could reduce the fall in output in Ireland by almost 4 percentage points in 2020.

detail.abstract: The Government’s fiscal response to COVID-19, cost of living pressures and humanitarian support for Ukraine resulted in an increase in government spending of €35 billion between 2020 and 2022. Despite this exceptional rise in expenditure, the headline budget balance returned to surplus in 2022, driven by windfall corporation tax revenue. If this excess corporation tax is excluded, the budget remained in deficit last year. The current macroeconomic environment – characterised by an economy at full employment and with high inflation – presents fresh challenges for fiscal policy. The analysis indicates that discretionary government spending increases or tax cuts above current plans would add to demand and inflation when the economy is already at full capacity. Moreover, the public finances face looming constraints over the medium term due to the need to increase public spending to address the long-term costs of ageing and climate change. Saving windfall taxes today would reduce – albeit not eliminate – the extent of future tax increases needed to fund these new demands on the public finances. Introducing measures to broaden the tax base could help to ease inflationary pressures while public capital spending is being ramped up and at the same time enhance the resilience of the public finances in the face of known future challenges.

detail.title: Economic Policy Uncertainty in Small Open Economies, a Case Study of Ireland

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 1

detail.abstract: The main contribution of this paper is the construction of a measure of Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU) for Ireland, following the methodology of Baker, Bloom and Davis (2016). The paper also sheds light on the implications of heightened uncertainty for Ireland, a small open economy operating within monetary union. Exogenous domestic uncertainty shocks foreshadow persistent declines in Irish investment and employment, with no clear response by the ECB. On the other hand, no such decline in demand is observed following global uncertainty shocks, largely resulting from an accommodative monetary policy stance by the ECB. Results from this paper suggest that policy uncertainty shocks have negative and persistent effects on Irish real economic activity, only when interest rates do not react, or are constrained. Common identification problems in the literature are also discussed and suggestions are made for future work in the area.

title: Parking fees as a tool for congestion management in natural areas: behavioural insights from complementary hypothetical and real experiments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Erasmus School of Health Policy & Management and University of Padua

detail.title: Parking fees as a tool for congestion management in natural areas: behavioural insights from complementary hypothetical and real experiments
detail.abstract: The increasing demand for recreational activities in natural areas has led to overtourism, ecological strain, and stakeholder conflicts. Parking fees have emerged as a potential tool to manage congestion and fund conservation, yet their implementation often faces resistance. This study investigates visitors’ responses to parking fees in the Cansiglio Forest (Northeastern Italy), by using a novel combination of stated preference (SP) and revealed preference (RP) experiments. The SP survey assessed hypothetical willingness to pay, while the RP experiment collected real payment data from designated parking areas, to assess the behavioral response of visitors to the introduction of such measure. Results revealed significant differences between the two methods: SP data indicated that most visitors would be willingness to pay up to €6, while the RP data showed strong resistance, with most visitors refusing to pay even a €1 fee. Regression analyses identified key factors influencing fee acceptability. Methodologically, this study contributes to the existing literature by designing a novel RP approach to collect real choice data and by demonstrating the advantages of employing SP and RP methods for robust policy insights. Empirically, it addresses the under-researched topic of using parking fees as a congestion management tool in natural areas, providing insights into both immediate resistance and potential long-term acceptance. These findings offer valuable guidance for policymakers aiming to implement sustainable tourism strategies which balance visitor satisfaction and environmental conservation.

detail.title: Blockholder exit threats and management tone manipulation: evidence from China

publicationDetails.detailsText: China Accounting & Finance Review, volume 28, issue 1, 2026
publicationDetails.journalName: China Accounting & Finance Review (CAFR)

detail.abstract:
Purpose-This study empirically examines the relationship between the blockholder exit threats (ETs) and management tone manipulation, based on two competing hypotheses: the "governance hypothesis" and the "market pressure hypothesis." The study aims to explore the impact and mechanisms of ETs on the quality of textual information disclosure. 

Design/methodology/approach-This study uses ordinary least squares multivariate regressions on panel data from Chinese A-share listed companies spanning 2007 to 2022. Building on Huang et al. (2014), we construct a benchmark model of managerial tone and use its residuals to measure abnormal positive tone. Blockholder exit threat (ET), following Dou et al. (2018), is proxied by the interaction between stock liquidity and blockholder competition. To address endogeneity, we employ propensity score matching, the Heckman two-stage method and lagged models. Robustness checks include alternative variable definitions and different textual dictionaries. 

Findings-The results show that external blockholder ETs significantly increase the degree of abnormal positive managerial tone, thereby supporting the market pressure hypothesis. Further analyses reveal that the positive association between ETs and abnormal positive tone is stronger in subsamples where managerial market pressure is higher, the level of blockholder expropriation is greater and insider trading is more prevalentindicating a stronger collusion motive between external blockholders and management. Mechanism tests show that ETs manipulate managerial tone by increasing the sensitivity of managerial wealth to share price fluctuations. 

Research limitations/implications-This study is limited to Chinese A-share listed companies, whose unique institutional and regulatory environment may restrict the generalizability of the findings to other markets. Differences in disclosure rules, legal enforcement and investor protection between China and developed economies suggest that the identified mechanisms may not apply universally. Additionally, our reliance on annual report narratives for measuring managerial tone may overlook other communication channels. Future research could extend the analysis to other market segments or countries and incorporate additional data sources to test the robustness and broader applicability of our conclusions.

Practical implications-The results highlight the need for enhanced regulatory oversight of narrative disclosures to prevent managerial “window dressing” and mitigate information asymmetry. Regulators should strengthen cross-validation between financial and non-financial information and promote mechanisms that increase the cost and risk of blockholder–management collusion. Investors are advised to critically assess managerial tone and remain alert to overly optimistic language. Additionally, increased supervision of tunneling and insider trading, along with stronger legal protections for minority shareholders, is essential for fostering transparency and integrity in China’s capital markets and improving overall market quality.

Originality/value-This paper contributes to understanding the impact of external blockholder ETs on managerial tone manipulation in narrative disclosures from the perspective of ownership structure in China’s unique institutional environment. The findings of the study provide new insights into the governance role of blockholders and offer policy implications for improving information transparency and the healthy development of emerging capital markets.

detail.title: Disciplinary effect of short selling: evidence from mergers and acquisitions

publicationDetails.detailsText: China Accounting & Finance Review, volume 28, issue 1, 2026
publicationDetails.journalName: China Accounting & Finance Review (CAFR)

detail.abstract:
Purpose-Using Regulation SHO's pilot program as a natural experiment, we study how removing short-selling constraints affects a firm's mergers and acquisitions (M&A). 

Design/methodology/approach-Difference-indifference (DID) regressions. 

Findings-We find that during the pilot program, firms in the pilot group significantly reduce their valuedestroying M&A activities. The disciplinary effect focuses on firms with higher levels of agency problems and those with higher levels of CEO incentive pay, where equity-based compensation increases managerial sensitivity to market discipline. The impact of the pilot program on M&As does not focus on overvalued firms, indicating that stock overvaluation does not channel the impact. Finally, we show that the M&A deal quality of firms in the pilot group improves during the pilot program. The overall results indicate that the removal of short sale constraints can create an effective external monitoring system for corporate investment behavior. 

Originality/value-Our paper contributes to the growing literature in several ways. First, our study extends Chang et al. (2019) to provide a different but equally important angle on how short selling disciplines M&As. Second, our results of using long-term post-acquisition stock performance supplement the study of Chang et al. (2019). Third, this paper extends Shi et al. (2021) to take advantage of the Regulation SHO's pilot program. Therefore, we investigate the effect of short selling on M&As from a policy perspective.

title: Tariffs and Firm Expectations
affiliations: ETH Zürich - KOF Swiss Economic Institute, ETH Zürich - KOF Swiss Economic Institute, ETH Zurich - CER-ETH -Center of Economic Research, ETH Zürich - KOF Swiss Economic Institute, ETH Zurich, ETH Zurich and ETH Zürich

detail.title: Tariffs and Firm Expectations

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how firms’ expectations respond to prospective tariff shocks using a randomized survey experiment among Swiss manufacturing firms. When confronted with potential U.S. tariffs, respondents expect sizable declines in turnover and investment, yet anticipate increases in ex-tariff export prices despite falling demand. This combination of declining activity and rising prices runs counter to the standard prediction of trade models, in which tariffs reduce foreign demand and put downward pressure on exporters’ prices. The observed pattern is consistent with a destination-specific cost-push mechanism, whereby tariffs raise exporters’ marginal costs through compliance burdens, logistical frictions, or reduced scale. Embedding firms’ stated price and sales expectations in a parsimonious structural pricing model, we quantify the implied cost changes and recover sector-level demand elasticities. The estimates indicate substantial heterogeneity across industries and are, on average, consistent with short-run trade elasticities from the recent literature. Moreover, we corroborate the experimental evidence using panel survey data on firms’ expectations around an unexpected U.S. tariff announcement.

detail.abstract:
Purpose-Central bank digital currencies (CBDC) are at the forefront of transformative digital finance, driven by central banks and policymakers worldwide. This paper sets out a hybrid systematic literature review (SLR), combining bibliometric analysis and the TCCM framework. 

Design/methodology/approach-The methodology involved analysis of 371 articles from the Scopus database, covering the period from 2012 until August 2024 through bibliometric analysis. In the next step, we followed the theories-characteristics-contexts-methods (TCCM) framework using a collection of 88 high-quality publications. Utilizing the TCCM framework, this study offers a qualitative overview to guide future research endeavors. 

Findings-The bibliometric analysis offers key statistics on publications, key trends, influential authors, reputable journals and statistical insights related to CBDC research. The TCCM framework provides major theories, variables, context and methodology. The key themes that emerge from our analysis include the design, pilot and implementation of CBDC highlighting both technological and regulatory challenges, Financial stability and monetary policy implications and user Perspectives on CBDC adoption taking into account factors such as accessibility, security and usability. 

Originality/value-The paper offers significant value in terms of undertaking a SLR by combining the bibliometric analysis and the TCCM framework. The study is conducted in a rapidly developing theme of CBDC.

title: Anthropocene Epistemology: Political, Ecological, and Economic Entanglements
affiliations: Ca’ Foscari University of Venice

detail.title: Anthropocene Epistemology: Political, Ecological, and Economic Entanglements

publicationDetails.detailsText: Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics Research Paper Series No. 05/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: Department of Economics, Ca' Foscari University of Venice Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This essay critically explores the connection between epistemology, political ecology, economy, and technological developments in the Anthropocene, understood as the epoch in which humankind has become a major force of geological transformation. It addresses the Anthropocene as a discourse and as a reality, bringing together epistemological reflexivity, ideology critique, and political economy-cum-ecology. The essay begins with an overview of the genesis and development of the Anthropocene concept-an often-repeated history which I reconsider from the viewpoint of historiographic developments in the history and philosophy of science. Since the Anthropocene hypothesis makes the history of knowledge, technological advancement, and socioeconomic structures fundamental factors in the Earth's history, I point to the necessity of revising our reality-conceptions to account for the development of a world in which epistemic, economic, and political histories intersect with physics, geology, and biology. As a reappraisal of the historico-materialist approaches to science studies, I propose to expand the 'externalist' understanding of the socioeconomic roots and social functions of science by including, in the geoanthropological paradigm to come, considerations of social metabolism and ecology. This proposal is also meant to serve as a basis for new forms of cross-disciplinary economic thinking that must comprise cultural and environmental perspectives. These considerations are the background of my criticism of the ideological aberrations in the debate on Anthropocene politics, which I term 'dark ecologies'. I especially refer to Bruno Latour's adherence to Malthusian and social-Darwinian ideas. In the last part, I discuss eco-socialist alternatives to the ecological impasse and advocate for the defence of the commons against their alienation as a premise of future prosperity.

title: Rural Agricultural Infrastructures and Sustainable Rural Development: Examining Nigeria's River Basin and Rural Development Authorities
affiliations: Rhema Univeristy, Nigeria. and Michael Okpara University of Agriculture - Department of Mechanical Engineering

detail.title: Rural Agricultural Infrastructures and Sustainable Rural Development: Examining Nigeria's River Basin and Rural Development Authorities
detail.abstract: River Basin and Rural Development Authorities were created in Nigeria to serve as catalyst for agricultural growth and sustainable rural development through the deployment of critical rural agricultural infrastructures. Provision of rural agricultural infrastructures is fundamental towards sustainable rural development and involves a holistic strategy for developing rural areas by managing available natural resources in a responsible and sustainable manner. This is necessary for improving the condition of life for present and future generations. Sustainable rural development is an approach which seeks to balance rural economic growth with social and environmental sustainability, and aiming to increase agricultural productivity and income of the rural poor, improve their living and working conditions through sustainable agriculture and diverse non-farm entrepreneurial opportunity created by well-functioning interventions in rural infrastructures to improve local governance through the establishment of transparent and accountable practices for public decision-making, implementation, operation and maintenance. Rural development through community-driven involvement can be critical to ensuring that rural roads remain passable through all seasons to enhance rural-urban connectivity. This is imperative because rural infrastructures in terms of rural transportation can play an important role in empowering poor people, linking isolated communities to the rest of the world, and giving rural communities greater access and influence over political and local governance processes and having the voice to ask for essential rural infrastructures, like rural electrification. Rural electrification is an important requirement for improving rural farm and non-farm productivity. It is a key requirement to improve agricultural mechanization and extension services to stimulate agro-industrial sustainable development. For example, the Anambra/Imo River Basin and Rural Development Authority has the responsibility for the Lower Anambra irrigation project with a gross area of 8000 hectres and a net area of 4000 hectres respectively. The project involves irrigation, drainage systems and rural road network development among others that brought development to the catchment areas where disposable income of individuals increased more than ten folds, and mode of housing, dressing, as well as literacy levels of the communities improved tremendously. This particular Authority was involved in dewatering permanently flooded areas, like the Ndiegoro flood project in Aba, Abia State, Nigeria. The qualitative exploratory research design was adopted for this investigation and the result showed significant positive relationship between rural agricultural infrastructures and sustainable rural development. This study recommends that governments should ensure the full revitalization, of the river basin and rural development approach for improving agricultural productivity in Nigeria. The study was never exhaustive due to paucity of research funding and relevant current literature. Further study should examine the relationship between mismanagement and low agricultural productivity in Nigeria.

title: Direct Gaussian Process Predictive Regressions with Mixed Frequency Data
affiliations: University of Salzburg, Bocconi University - Department of Economics, Vienna University of Economics and Business - Department of Economics and Vienna University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Direct Gaussian Process Predictive Regressions with Mixed Frequency Data

publicationDetails.journalName: BAFFI Centre on Economics, Finance & Regulation Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We develop Bayesian machine learning methods for mixed frequency data. This involves handling frequency mismatches and specifying functional relationships between (possibly many) predictors and low frequency dependent variables. We use Gaussian Processes (GPs) in direct nonlinear predictive regressions, and compress higher frequency variables in a structured way. This yields a set of kernels for GPs with distinct properties and implications. We evaluate the proposed framework in an out-of-sample exercise focusing on quarterly US GDP growth and inflation. Our approach leverages high-dimensional mixed frequency data in a computationally efficient way, and offers robustness and gains in predictive accuracy along several dimensions.

title: The Economics of Tariffs
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department of Economics and Stanford University

detail.title: The Economics of Tariffs

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
A central insight from neoclassical economics is that international trade operates like an improvement in production technology. It generates mutual aggregate welfare gains for countries as a whole, but creates winners and losers within countries. Tariffs are a tax on this trading technology and distort the prices faced by domestic consumers and producers. Large countries can use tariffs to improve their terms of trade on world markets. But if all countries try to do so, they can end up with lower welfare than if they cooperated to liberalize trade. Tariffs can be used to redistribute income between the winners and losers from trade within countries. But there can be other more efficient ways to achieve redistribution. Policies to promote economic activity in critical industries can be rationalized based on externalities or national security. But these arguments typically rationalize targeted policies towards those industries and tariffs can be dominated by other policy interventions. Empirical findings from the recent waves of U.S. tariffs suggest that most of the incidence of these tariffs has been borne by U.S. importers, wholesalers, retailers and consumers rather than by foreign exporters. These tariffs have led to a large-scale reorganization of U.S. supply chains away from China to third countries. Although this reorganization has substantially reduced China's share of U.S. imports, the U.S. remains indirectly exposed to China through the imports of these third countries.

title: From Information Asymmetry to Knowledge Asymmetry: Order Flow, Market Inelasticity, and Asset Pricing
affiliations: University of Trento

detail.title: From Information Asymmetry to Knowledge Asymmetry: Order Flow, Market Inelasticity, and Asset Pricing
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified framework for asset-price formation that integrates the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH), the Inelastic Market Hypothesis (IMH), and two complementary sources of heterogeneity: asymmetric information (AI) and asymmetric knowledge (AK). While EMH describes prices as efficient aggregators of information, IMH highlights that limited arbitrage capacity and institutional constraints render aggregate demand for risky assets highly inelastic, so that order flows exert a persistent price impact. Building on this insight, the paper formalizes how AI and AK jointly shape trader expectations and order submission. AI captures differences in signal precision and timing, whereas AK reflects heterogeneity in interpretation, modeling sophistication, and technological capacity. These asymmetries generate structured and persistent order-flow imbalances that propagate through an inelastic liquidity channel, producing excess volatility, long memory in returns, and permanent price effects. Aggregation yields two distinct order-flow components, a fast-moving informational factor and a slowmoving knowledge-dispersion factor, which enter asset returns alongside the market factor. The resulting framework extends standard asset-pricing models by introducing order-flow and knowledge-asymmetry risk factors, implying that market efficiency is conditional on the distribution of informational access and cognitivetechnological capabilities among market participants.

title: Climate Disasters and Intergenerational Equity: A Fiscal Rule for Sustainable Development
affiliations: Columbia University, Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, Department of Economics, National University Singapore and Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Climate Disasters and Intergenerational Equity: A Fiscal Rule for Sustainable Development

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Climate disasters threaten intergenerational equity by exposing future generations to rising risks. We develop a model in which a government learns about disaster risk and enforces a sustainability criterion requiring expected social welfare to be non-decreasing over time. This criterion—similar to the principle underlying the UN Sustainable Development Goals—can be decentralized through state-contingent fiscal instruments: when perceived disaster risk is high, the constraint binds and government raises a consumption tax to finance investment subsidies for resilience. Such a fiscal rule leads to intergenerational-welfare smoothing and improves asset valuations despite adverse climate news due to commitments to future resilience. Compared with a government that adopts a social discount rate lower than households’, the sustainability-constraint rule responds to disaster risk and is better aligned with observed consumption-based climate-resilience taxes, such as those implemented in Greece and Spain.

title: Are Macro Shocks Second Order?
affiliations: University of Piraeus - Department of Banking and Financial Management, Babson College and Boston University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Are Macro Shocks Second Order?

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This paper addresses two fundamental macroeconomics questions. First, are macro shocks large enough to alter the course of the economy? Second, are they large enough to materially impact economic welfare? Lucas and many others have addressed these issues, but do so primarily in the context of representative agent models. We study these questions using a large-scale, general equilibrium, stochastic, overlapping generations model. We consider 80 generations overlapping in an economy buffeted by realistically calibrated total factor productivity and capital depreciation shocks. The model is solved using Marcet’s projection method taking explicit account of the full state space, which comprises 81 variables. Our findings, some recapitulated from prior studies by Hasanhodzic and Kotlikoff, suggest macro shocks are second order both with respect to their impact on aggregate variables and individual welfare. Specifically, the probability that the stochastic economy’s long-run aggregates materially deviate from their deterministic counterparts is less than one percent. Furthermore, the realized (simulated) lifetime utility of generations born in the long run rarely differs from deterministic long-run utility levels by more than 1 percent, measured as consumption-compensating differentials. These findings are supported by the model’s small equity premium. Moreover, they are essentially indifferent to the presence of a bond market. Both results suggest agents are minimally concerned with precautionary savings against these shocks. Our RBC-in-OLG findings suggest that what really moves the macroeconomy and demands attention is policy, not shocks.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Project Lithos: Deterministic Mapping of Absolute Mineral Concentrations in Arkansas and New York
affiliations: Founder, Unified Principle

detail.title: Project Lithos: Deterministic Mapping of Absolute Mineral Concentrations in Arkansas and New York
detail.abstract: This paper presents a deterministic methodology for locating the maximum concentrations of diamonds and Herkimer crystals in the United States. Traditional prospecting relies on stochastic methods, including soil sampling and surface observations. In contrast, the approach presented here-Project Lithos-applies the Unified Principle to integrate multi-layered datasets, including historical recoveries, terrain construction, hydrological and hydrothermal vectors, and volumetric analysis of undrawn reserves. By synthesizing these layers into a singular computational framework, the model resolves to a pre-verified, absolute coordinate of maximum sub-surface concentration for each site. The results offer operational-ready geospatial maps for immediate field application and demonstrate the efficacy of deterministic modeling in mineral prospecting.

title: From Imposition to Lifting: Estimating the Effects of Sanctions Over Their Lifecycle
affiliations: Drexel University, Deutsche Bundesbank - Economics Department,  and Drexel University - Department of Economics & International Business

detail.title: From Imposition to Lifting: Estimating the Effects of Sanctions Over Their Lifecycle

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We combine the latest difference-in-differences estimators for treatments with exit and structural gravity literature to evaluate the effects of sanctions on trade, when they are in place and when they are lifted. Our analysis shows that sanctions reduce trade between senders and targets by 58%, with estimates from our preferred model 50% larger than those from traditional two-way fixed effects (TWFE) models. A bias decomposition highlights arbitrary weighting and contamination bias in TWFE estimates. Sensitivity checks confirm the robustness of our findings, emphasizing the relevance of these methods for gravity estimations, including trade, migration, foreign investment, and other bilateral flows.

title: The Non-CO2 Aviation Emissions: How to Regulate the Elephant in the Room
affiliations: KU Leuven - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Non-CO2 Aviation Emissions: How to Regulate the Elephant in the Room

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: The non-CO2 aviation emissions (mainly contrails) can, in total, be up to twice as damaging for climate as the CO2 emissions associated to the use of kerosene. As the warming effect of the non-CO2 emissions depends strongly on metereological conditions, it is difficult to attribute the non-CO2 warming effect to a particular flight. Without detailed meteorological information per fight only a blunt emission permit or tax system that taxes all kerosene used in aviation at two to three times the current damage estimate of CO2 could work. Even if this can be justified from an environmental economics point of view, this risks to be unacceptable for the aviation sector. The result is that there is, at present, no active non-CO2 policy. The aviation industry has proposed a 20 year plan to improve the monitoring of these emissions before taking action to address the non-CO2 emissions. We propose a multi-period regulation scheme to address this problem much faster. In the first stage, airlines and public sector agencies are subsidized to improve measurements. These measurement inputs are used to construct a contrail forecasting model. In the second stage, the model is used to propose alternative flight-paths. Airlines are incentivized to adopt the new flightpaths by subsidies that cover the additional flight operation costs. A numerical illustration for the wider EU-region shows that the mechanism proposed can lead to significant climate emission savings that are larger than the savings of CO2 emissions that result from the introduction of ETS or Sustainable Aviation Fuels for aviation.

title: The AI Epistemic Trap™: A Framework for Governance Under Contested Truth
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The AI Epistemic Trap™: A Framework for Governance Under Contested Truth
detail.abstract:
As Artificial Intelligence moves from objective tasks to complex decision-making, governance must shift from data cleaning to navigating "worldview divergence." This paper introduces The AI Epistemic Trap™, a phenomenon where AI systems default to a "Tyranny of the Crowd" by averaging incompatible expert opinions, thereby eroding an organization's strategic intent.

We present a Taxonomy of Disagreement to help governors distinguish between "Measurement Noise" (reducible errors) and "Framework Divergence" (irreducible worldviews). To quantify this risk, we propose a mathematical formalization of Epistemic Divergence ($\Delta E$), measuring the gap between a model’s consensus-based output and the organization's specific strategic requirements ($E\Phi(\omega) $).

Through a case study analysis of a $40M strategic failure, we demonstrate that traditional accuracy metrics fail in contested domains like finance, medical diagnostics, and recruitment. We conclude by detailing the Epistemic Stress Test, a five-step governance protocol featuring "Framework Enumeration" and "Context Recognition Testing." This conceptual framework provides a roadmap for institutions—ranging from academic research centers to enterprise boards—to ensure AI alignment not just with general data, but with the specific "Truth Frameworks" required for mission-critical operations.

title: How Does the Number of Attribute Ratings Affect a Product’s Overall Rating? Evidence From Tripadvisor
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology, Temple University - Fox School of Business and Management, Harbin Institute of Technology, University of Warwick and Harbin Institute of Technology

detail.title: How Does the Number of Attribute Ratings Affect a Product’s Overall Rating? Evidence From Tripadvisor
detail.abstract: A product's overall rating serves as a quality indicator for prospective consumers, with the online rating system's design playing a critical role. However, it remains unclear how the number of attribute ratings that consumers assign informs overall ratings. To address this issue, we examined secondary data collected from online hotel reviews and conducted a randomized experiment. Results showed that consumers who provide more attribute ratings tend to give higher and less extreme overall ratings. More precisely, the presence of multiple attribute rating channels discourages consumers from transferring their evaluations of specific attributes to a product's or service's overall rating. Temporal distance and review photos were found to moderate these relationships. Our research contributes to the literature by clarifying how the number of attribute ratings shapes consumers' overall rating behavior. We offer corresponding suggestions for online sellers to develop more effective rating management strategies.

title: Regional Favoritism: New Data, Larger Sample, Same Pattern
affiliations: , University of St. Gallen and

detail.title: Regional Favoritism: New Data, Larger Sample, Same Pattern

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Hodler and Raschky (2014) provide evidence for regional favoritism by documenting that subnational regions have more intense nighttime lights when they are the birth region of the country's current political leader than at other times. In this paper, we test the robustness of their findings using new data on nighttime light emissions and the birthplaces of political leaders, resulting in a larger sample with many more countries and years. We confirm that leader birth regions have more intense nighttime lights and that this effect is larger in countries with high ethnic fractionalization, undemocratic institutions, and low levels of education.

title: Managing Risks and Building Resilience in the Public Finances

detail.title: Managing Risks and Building Resilience in the Public Finances

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 2
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Strong economic growth and exceptional corporation tax receipts have benefitted the public finances over the last decade but these benign conditions are threatened. Risks to the public finances and the economy from Ireland’s reliance on multinational firms have risen given recent developments in the US and the more disruptive international economic environment. A loss of corporation tax – most notably, of the windfall receipts of recent years – along with weaker economic growth and lower multinational investment would result in a deficit in the public finances of over 4 per cent of national income by 2030, in the absence of corrective action. To improve long-term growth and the resilience of the economy, increases in public investment that address current infrastructure gaps are needed. These should be implemented in a way that is consistent with long-run economic and fiscal sustainability. With current full-employment conditions and in the absence of offsetting revenue-raising measures, further large increases in public investment on top of existing plans could aggravate overheating pressures. If economic activity slows markedly, then increases in public investment could be accommodated with lower inflationary risks and would help to support demand. Implementing measures to broaden the tax base would improve the resilience of the public finances should CT revenue decline. Moreover, it would help to ensure that growing public expenditure needs from an ageing population, to fund new infrastructure and to meet emission reduction targets can be sustainably met.

title: The Standards Advantage: How Data Interoperability Could Lift Europe's Screen Economies
affiliations: Tallinn University (TLU)

detail.title: The Standards Advantage: How Data Interoperability Could Lift Europe's Screen Economies

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the European Commission [grant number 101094988].

contentFormat.other: It is a research project report.

detail.abstract:
Purpose. This report provides an evidence-based roadmap for adopting data standards that raise the effectiveness and competitiveness of Europe’s film industries. It focuses on standards that reduce friction across production, distribution, and cross-border collaboration, with special attention to ease of uptake for SMEs and small-country markets. The recommendations align with the EU’s data policy direction – Data Governance Act, European data spaces, eIDAS 2 – and with the CresCine objective to turn Europe’s cultural diversity into a market advantage.

Problem: Too many European workflows still run on bespoke spreadsheets and siloed databases; rights data are opaque, identifiers are fragmented and deliverables vary by counterparty – slowing licensing, inflating costs and limiting circulation.

Why this matters for competitiveness: These standards shrink time-to-market, curb versioning and quality control overhead, make avails machine-actionable, and enable consistent analytics. For SMEs, the pay-off is the ability to participate in pan-EU releases without bespoke rework and to demonstrate availability and compliance quickly to buyers and platforms. For small countries, multilingual linked-data practices increase discoverability and reduce the cost of operating across languages.

title: Conflict Intensity and Entrepreneurial Intentions: Evidence from Iraqi Regions
affiliations: Western Sydney University, Lebanese American University and University of Marburg - Center for Near and Middle Eastern Studies (CNMS)

detail.title: Conflict Intensity and Entrepreneurial Intentions: Evidence from Iraqi Regions

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between conflict events, conflict-related fatalities, and entrepreneurial intentions in Iraq, one of the most war-affected countries over the past four decades and a context largely overlooked in the entrepreneurship literature. By combining regional-level data from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) with individual-level data from the World Values Survey (WVS), we find that, controlling for other factors, entrepreneurial intentions are significantly lower in regions experiencing higher levels of conflicts and fatalities. This finding is robust across multiple estimation methods and model specifications. Furthermore, our results indicate that financially stable individuals show a sharper decline in entrepreneurial intentions in response to conflicts compared to financially vulnerable individuals.

title: The Foreign Exchange and Over-the-counter Interest Rate Derivatives Market in Ireland – Results of the BIS Triennial Survey 2019

detail.title: The Foreign Exchange and Over-the-counter Interest Rate Derivatives Market in Ireland – Results of the BIS Triennial Survey 2019

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. QB1
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The Central Bank of Ireland participated in the most recent survey of global turnover in foreign exchange (FX) and over-the-counter (OTC) single- currency interest rate derivatives that the Bank of International Settlements (BIS) coordinates every three years. The survey is a key source of information on the size and structure of global FX and OTC interest rate derivatives markets. Ireland has participated since 1995, collecting comprehensive information on the activities of credit institutions’ derivatives sales desks that are resident in Ireland. Given the international character of derivatives markets, such information is of interest from a supervisory perspective and can provide additional information about external financial stability risks facing the Irish economy through the lens of financial market activity. The 2019 survey results for Ireland show a substantial increase in FX and OTC interest rate derivatives trading during the last three years. The Irish trading volumes recovered from the downward trend recorded in the previous two surveys, and the growth rate of Irish derivatives turnover between 2016 and 2019 outpaced the global growth rate. As this article will show, the main factor behind the strong Irish growth was that large global derivatives dealers opened or reactivated derivatives sales desks in Ireland as part of their overall business strategy and in preparation for Brexit. Other driving factors also contributed to the strong growth between 2016 and 2019. For example, the rise in electronic and automated trading facilitated the growth of trading both in foreign exchange and in over-the-counter interest rate derivatives markets, and increased the participation of non-bank dealers in both markets. The growth in the FX market was mainly driven by an increase in FX swaps, used for hedging foreign exchange risks and managing funding liquidity, in an environment of increasing economic uncertainties and excess liquidity in the euro area. The growth in US dollar and euro trading outpaced the growth in pound sterling. OTC interest rate derivatives markets additionally benefited from structural developments like clearing and compression, and from changing expectations about US short-term interest rates that incentivised hedging and speculation activities.

title: Public vs. Private Information under Fixed Total Precision
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Public vs. Private Information under Fixed Total Precision
detail.abstract: We study Gaussian coordination games under a strict conservation-of-precision constraint: total signal precision K is fixed and must be split between one public signal and two private signals. Each agent’s effective precision therefore remains constant at K/2 regardless of the allocation \lambda \in [0,1]. We prove that coordination efficiency (negative expected action dispersion) is strictly concave in the public-precision share \lambda, achieving a unique interior maximum at \lambda^* \in (0,1). The optimal \lambda^* rises monotonically with the strength of strategic complementarities. The framework reconciles the conflicting welfare conclusions of Morris–Shin (2002) and Angeletos–Pavan (2007) by isolating the pure allocation effect from changes in total information. Applications to central-bank transparency, blockchain consensus, and bandwidth-constrained federated learning are discussed, with Bitcoin and Ethereum serving as real-world illustrations.

detail.title: Managing the Public Finances in Uncertain Times

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. QB3

detail.abstract: The pandemic had a major impact on the public finances, resulting in an exceptional €27 billion increase in government spending up to 2021 and adding to the national debt. As the pandemic has abated, the public finances have recovered quickly. The war in Ukraine presents fresh challenges, with high inflation and new expenditure pressures adding to existing demands on the public finances. Against a backdrop of supply-side constraints and with large increases in capital spending already planned out to 2025, the analysis here shows that additional permanent current spending funded by borrowing would add to inflationary pressures and slow down the projected recovery in the public finances. These effects would be mitigated if the spending was funded by raising revenue. Lower corporation tax revenue, higher interest rates and slower growth would result in the persistence of more elevated government debt over the medium term. In the current high inflation environment, careful management of the public finances is required to ensure sustainable economic growth and to rebuild resilience in the government’s finances following successive negative shocks.

detail.title: Optimizing Simplified Payment Verification for Electronic Cash: An Economic and Game-Theoretic Framework for Low-Bandwidth SPV Systems in Blockchain-Based Payment Networks
detail.abstract: We propose a low-bandwidth SPV payment protocol enabling offline customer wallets to transact at merchant point-of-sale terminals without requiring direct network connectivity for the payer, extending blockchain payments to resource-constrained devices such as smart cards. The protocol achieves sub-15 ms cryptographic verification (Merkle path + signature check) with an optional seconds-scale alert window, through a layered detection architecture comprising UTXO Seen Datasets, overlay push alerts, and key-value proof databases, and we formally prove its correctness and security. We distinguish two structurally different double-spend strategies-secret-chain reorganization and broadcast racing-and prove that the detection layers can suppress the broadcast-attack class below the reorg floor when detection quality is sufficient (P eff race ≤ P reorg (q, z)), leaving the Nakamoto bound as the residual risk floor. Three analytical contributions characterize the architecture: an impossibility frontier, an optimal channel allocation theorem with a ratio upper-bound proof, and an endpoint corruption theorem establishing adversarial deterrence conditions. A split-wallet architecture with a master SPV node coordinates multiple merchant terminals. Drawing on transaction cost economics and information economics, we formalize the economic friction inherent in SPV systems. Game-theoretic models-including Stackelberg, Nash, Cournot, Bayesian, and stochastic games-characterize strategic interactions with formal equilibrium proofs. Monte Carlo simulations with 200 000 trials validate the analytical bounds.

detail.abstract: Screening human capital based on signals such as job applications or entrepreneurial pitches is crucial for organizations. Signals are often informative insofar as they require differential knowledge and effort to produce. Generative AI (GAI) complicates screening by lowering the cost of producing impressive signals. We model the informational effects of GAI, showing that applicants' access to GAI can increase - but also decrease - an evaluator's screening mistakes. This result depends on how GAI affects experts' signals compared to non-experts'. Using experiments in hiring and startup investing, we estimate that senders' access to GAI (ChatGPT) lowers screening accuracy by 4-9% for employers and startup investors. Consistent with our model, senders' access to GAI also improves screening accuracy in some settings - in our case, among senders from non-English-speaking countries. These results show that GAI can profoundly shape screening accuracy.

title: Narcissism Theory and the Goldwater Rule: An Empirical and Interdisciplinary Analysis

detail.title: Narcissism Theory and the Goldwater Rule: An Empirical and Interdisciplinary Analysis

publicationDetails.journalName: Emory University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Recent years have seen a surge of interest in the “Goldwater rule,” which affects whether and to what extent psychiatrists can weigh in on the mental health of a public figure. The rule has been invoked to limit expert opinion on a variety of matters ranging from political candidates’ suitability for public office to whether already-elected officials remain mentally fit for duty.

While the Goldwater rule may have made sense when it was adopted sixty years ago, much has changed since then. In particular, recent years have seen the rise of a new field of interdisciplinary study known as narcissism theory, which analyzes, among other things, the effects that political leaders suffering from narcissism have on foreign policy and international relations.

This Article considers whether narcissism theory provides a compelling reason to revise or revoke the Goldwater rule, particularly in light of recent events involving Venezuela, Iran, and Greenland.  In so doing, the Article introduces an extensive body of empirical research about the nature of narcissism, the link between narcissism and both interpersonal and international aggression, and the behavior of narcissistic politicians on the world stage. The discussion also considers whether there are any realistic means of mitigating problematic and dangerous behavior by narcissistic political leaders. When viewed as a whole, the empirical data strongly suggests an immediate need to revisit the Goldwater rule to allow expert opinion on narcissism to inform democratic debate.

detail.title: ESG ratings inconsistency and its effects on information in capital market

publicationDetails.journalName: China Accounting & Finance Review (CAFR)

detail.abstract:
Purpose-This study explores how inconsistency in environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings affects the information environment of publicly traded companies in emerging markets. 

Design/methodology/approach-Drawing on data from six ESG rating agencies covering listed Chinese firms from 2010 to 2022, we construct measures of pairwise ESG rating divergence and average them across 15 unique rater pairs. We then employ a battery of econometric methods to examine how inconsistencies in ESG ratings affect stock return synchronicity in the Chinese capital market. 

Findings-Our findings indicate that greater ESG rating divergence correlates with increased stock return synchronicity, suggesting a decline in the dissemination of firm-specific information. Supporting evidence for this relationship includes reduced private information flow, heightened opportunistic executive sales and decreased stock turnover for firms associated with higher ESG rating divergence. Our analysis suggests that such divergence hinders informed trading by institutional investors and the effect is more pronounced for firms with lower transparency, such as those with fewer analysts, limited investor oversight and sparse ESG disclosure, as well as for firms in non-polluting industries. These findings emphasize that ESG rating divergence exacerbates uncertainty about firms' future performance, discourages informed trading and ultimately restricts the integration of firm-specific information into stock prices. 

Originality/value-This study adds to the literature on ESG ratings and market efficiency by highlighting the importance of standardizing rating methodologies and improving corporate disclosure to counteract the adverse impacts of rating divergence.

title: Impact of Gender Imbalance on Workforce Efficiency and Productivity in Indian Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)

detail.title: Impact of Gender Imbalance on Workforce Efficiency and Productivity in Indian Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)
detail.abstract: Our study observes that gender imbalance remains a critical challenge in Indian Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), particularly in Coal India, Steel PSUs, and similar organizations. Out of approximately 2.25 lakh employees in Coal India, women constitute less than 10%, indicating severe underrepresentation and a workforce far from even an 80:20 gender ratio (Coal India Ltd., 2023; Ministry of Coal, 2022). Operational roles such as dozer operators, dumper operators, and shovel operators are overwhelmingly held by men, with only one or two women operators in rare cases. A similar imbalance exists in office and administrative positions, and most departments across PSUs exhibit very poor gender representation. Except for Kerala, most Indian states face a shortage of well-balanced gender representation (Singh & Sharma, 2021). Improving this ratio could bring substantial benefits to the workplace, including enhanced team dynamics, employee morale, energy levels, collaboration, and overall productivity (Catalyst, 2020; McKinsey & Company, 2022). It would also foster a safer and more respectful work environment, potentially reducing instances of sexual harassment or gender-based confrontation (UN Women, 2019). Hypothetically, if the gender ratio were improved to 1:1, it could create a transformative, almost 'paradise-like' scenarioleading to higher production, improved efficiency, achievement of organizational goals, negligible attrition rates, and highly motivated human resources. We argue that achieving a balanced gender ratio could make Human Resource Management more efficient and effective, serving as a key driver of workforce engagement and organizational excellence in Indian PSUs (ILO, 2021).

title: Do institutional investors exploit expectation errors in value/ glamour stocks?
affiliations: Fordham University, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Do institutional investors exploit expectation errors in value/ glamour stocks?

publicationDetails.detailsText: China Accounting & Finance Review, volume 28, issue 1, 2026
publicationDetails.journalName: China Accounting & Finance Review (CAFR)

detail.abstract:
Purpose-This study examines the institutional demand for mispriced stocks with incongruent expectations implied by the book-to-market (BM) ratio and financial strength. 

Design/methodology/approach-Institutional trading (or institutional demand) is calculated by both changes in institutional ownership (percentage of shares held) and the number of institutional investors from the previous to the current quarter. Market mispricing and expectation errors in value/glamour stocks can be identified by analysing firms' recent financial strength (measured by FSCORE). Firms are sorted into value stocks (top 30%), middle stocks (between 30% and 70%) and glamour stocks (bottom 30%) by distribution of BM ratios at the end of the previous fiscal year. Firms in the sample are then double sorted by FSCORE and BM: in each BM portfolio, firms are further classified into high-, mid-and low-FSCORE groups. 

Findings-Consistent with the argument of expectation errors in value/glamour stocks (Piotroski and So, 2012), institutional investors buy value stocks with strong fundamentals (underpriced) and sell glamour stocks with weak fundamentals (overpriced). Independent institutions are more likely to take advantage of the mispricing in value/glamour firms than passive institutions. Institutional trading on expectation errors could reduce the abnormal returns to mispriced stocks. Institutional trading patterns on mispriced value/glamour stocks are also documented in global markets. 

Originality/value-Our research provides new evidence that the institutional investors do exploit the BM anomalies if the mispricing can be identified by both the BM and the recent financial strength. Our study differs from Caglayan, Celiker and Sonaer (2018) as we emphasise that financial institutions, in addition to relying on only the BM values, process information from financial statements to infer firms' financial strength. This study is also the first to document that institutional demand on mispricing could attenuate the BM anomaly.

detail.title: The Sign-Normalized Position Ledger (De-Conflating the Double-Entry General Ledger)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Yuanjia Co (Sichuan, China)
declarations.funderStatement: Yuanjia Co (Sichuan, China)

detail.abstract: We describe a novel accounting system discovered in a practitioner-built Excel workbook. Through analysis of its architecture, we identify that the traditional double-entry general ledger is a multiply-conflated encoding that entangles at least five independent concerns into a single mechanism. The system under study systematically de-conflates them through a remarkably simple device: a dual-measure journal comprising Bal (each account's position in its own natural direction) and NetBal = IF(BSLv0="A", +1,-1) × Bal (the same entry sign-normalized to the owner's perspective). This single transformation, combined with a dimensional classification structure, separates: (1) the entity perspective from the owner perspective, (2) position measurement from income measurement, (3) economic nature from human purpose, (4) the transaction record from the analytical warehouse, and (5) accounting structure from user input. Each de-conflation removes a layer of infrastructure that traditional accounting requires-nominal accounts, closing entries, trial balance reconciliation, ETL processes, and debit/credit literacywhile preserving full financial reporting capability. We situate this work relative to Pacioli (1494), McCarthy's REA (1982), and dimensional modeling, arguing that the system represents the first identification of double-entry as a multiply-conflated encoding and the first demonstration that it can be systematically decomposed without loss of information.

detail.abstract:
Happiness research has generated a growing body of literature across disciplines, yet remains fragmented in terminology, concepts, and methods. This review addresses the need for an integrative framework that synthesizes key findings guided by the question: How is happiness conceptualized and operationalized across disciplines, and what are its main determinants and outcomes? An integrative literature review was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, Dimensions, and OpenAlex. The 230 most-cited articles in happiness and well-being research were selected using an index of absolute and field-normalized citation impact. Conceptual framework analysis was applied to synthesize concepts, measurements, and correlates. 

Findings are structured across micro, meso, and macro levels, and disciplines like (organizational) psychology, neurobiology, education, sociology, public health, economics, and political science. Concepts are classified as subjectivist or objectivist, and determinants as external, dispositional, interactionist, or intentional. Key psychological constructs include subjective well-being (cognitive and affective happiness) and psychological well-being (eudaimonic happiness), with broader concepts such as flourishing and thriving integrating both hedonic and eudaimonic aspects. Organizational psychology reflects similar distinctions of affective, cognitive, and eudaimonic concepts such as cognitive job satisfaction, moods at work, or work engagement. Subjectivist concepts are typically measured by global or domain-specific self-reports, while economists and sociologists examine objective correlates such as income, culture, sustainability, etc. At the political level, both perspectives feed into multidimensional policy indicators and education policies. However, conceptual vagueness and inconsistencies, as well as a predominant focus on hedonic measures indicate the need for conceptual differentiation and more holistic, robust measures. 

The resulting Integrative Framework of Happiness and Well-Being supports future research by offering conceptual clarity and measurement guidance, and by fostering interdisciplinary dialogue. By summarizing key findings on happiness in a comprehensive and accessible way, the framework also provides practical orientation for the public, promoting happiness as both a personal and social competence.

detail.abstract: Traditional analyses of monopoly power emphasize market concentration, pricing power, and firm size. This paper advances an alternative framework by examining invisible monopolies, forms of non-market power exercised through regulatory capture, standard-setting dominance, infrastructural control, data asymmetries, and institutional gatekeeping. We argue that in modern capitalism, durable economic power increasingly arises outside observable market transactions, operating instead through political, legal, and informational channels that shape competition ex ante. Drawing on insights from political economy, industrial organization, and institutional economics, the paper synthesizes existing literature to conceptualize non-market power as a central mechanism of value extraction and competitive insulation. We propose a structured typology of invisible monopolistic mechanisms and outline empirical strategies leveraging regulatory data, network analysis, procurement records, and lobbying disclosures to operationalize their measurement. The analysis highlights how non-market monopolies distort innovation incentives, entrench incumbency advantages, and weaken the effectiveness of conventional antitrust enforcement. By reframing monopoly power beyond price and output effects, this paper contributes to ongoing debates on market governance and regulatory design, and offers a foundation for policy interventions aimed at restoring contestability in contemporary capitalist systems.

title: Huge-Scale Assortment Optimization with Customer Choice: A Parallel Primal-Dual Approach

detail.title: Huge-Scale Assortment Optimization with Customer Choice: A Parallel Primal-Dual Approach
detail.abstract: We study huge-scale assortment optimization problems to maximize expected revenue under customer choice, addressing a fundamental challenge in industries such as transportation, retail, and healthcare. The choicebased linear programming (CBLP) formulation provides a powerful framework for optimizing sales allocations across customer segments, yet traditional approaches often fail to solve CBLPs of huge scale (involving millions of customer choices) due to the lack of algorithmic designs that exploit problem structure. To overcome this computational bottleneck, we propose a first-order primal-dual method, SPFOM, which requires only a small computational cost per iteration, achieves a provably near-optimal convergence rate, and can be readily extended to parallel computing environments. Computational experiments demonstrate the computational and practical superiority of SPFOM over state-of-the-art solvers for large-scale linear programs. The framework is extended to a multi-period assortment optimization setting with inventory constraints, where SPFOM estimates global shadow prices that enhance classical bid-price control policies compared with benchmark methods such as market segment decomposition. Numerical experiments and a case study using real-world data from the ZOZOTOWN platform validate the practical effectiveness of SPFOM, highlighting its advantages in improving revenue performance while maintaining balanced inventory levels.

detail.title: Impact of Generative AI on Organizational Innovation
detail.abstract:
This paper will explore the ways in which generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming the organizational innovation capacity, speed, and quality, specifically the initiation of emerging general-purpose innovation technology (Holmstrom and Carroll, 2024). The performance of innovation is becoming more determinant in competitive and dynamic contexts, where businesses have to quickly create, develop, and commercialize new concepts in order to maintain the lead (Machkour and Abriane, 2025). The main purpose of this article is to examine how GenAI works, the organizational and environmental environment that conditions its use, the risks that will be followed, and the quantifiable innovation benefits that will ensue from its application (Xu et al., 2024).
The methodology used in the study is a critical synthesis and conceptual integration of multidisciplinary literature based on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, the theory of innovation flow, and organizational learning perspectives (Al-Khatib, 2023; Catta-Preta et al., 2025; Lenart, 2025). It has been analyzed that the ideation throughput is
greatly improved by GenAI, prototyping is quickened, and novel types of cross-functional knowledge recombination are facilitated (Gindert and Muller, 2024; Holmstrom and Carroll, 2024). But the gains of innovation are not equal; they also highly rely on the quality of input content, user experience, skills, and the organizational and institutional environment (Xu et al.,2024).
Additionally, value creation can be restricted by ethical, legal, and governance limitations, especially those associated with trust, data integrity, and accountability, when they are improperly handled (Wamba et al., 2025; Piller et al., 2024). The research concludes that GenAI is a potent driver of innovation, and its advantages depend on the organization's preparation and its ability to develop and provide responsible governance (Kumar et al., 2025; Wamba et al., 2025). The article provides a synthesized notion and has practical managerial implications for harnessing GenAI in innovation systems.

detail.abstract: Following the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government on 5 August 2024, public universities in Bangladesh initiated a series of disciplinary actions that disproportionately targeted students affiliated with the Bangladesh Students' League (BSL). This study examines whether these actions conformed to principles of procedural fairness, administrative neutrality, and international human rights standards during a period of political transition. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the research integrates documentary analysis of official university decisions and media reports with first-hand qualitative evidence derived from direct, personally collected testimonies of affected students. The findings reveal pervasive perceptions of political bias within university disciplinary processes, manifested through non-neutral administrative conduct, politicized inquiry mechanisms, and inconsistent application of institutional regulations. Comparative evidence indicates selective enforcement, whereby students perceived as politically disfavored faced severe sanctions, while similarly situated students aligned with rival political organizations encountered lenient or negligible consequences, including in cases involving serious misconduct. These patterns suggest systemic procedural irregularities rather than isolated administrative failures. The study argues that such practices represent an extension of broader post-transition political repression into academic institutions, undermining students' rights to education, due process, and academic freedom. The article concludes by emphasizing the urgent need for transparent, legally grounded, and politically independent disciplinary frameworks to protect higher education from partisan capture in transitional political contexts.

detail.abstract: The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) is central to achieving sustainable transportation and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. However, the environmental benefits of EVs are heavily influenced by the sources of electricity used for their charging. This research paper explores the integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power, into the electric vehicle charging infrastructure. It evaluates the technical and economic feasibility of utilizing these renewable energies to create a sustainable charging ecosystem. The study analyzes existing models of solar-powered charging stations and wind-integrated solutions, assessing their reliability, efficiency, and scalability. Furthermore, it examines the role of smart grid technology in optimizing the integration of renewables with EV charging, focusing on energy management systems that enhance grid stability while promoting renewable energy utilization. Challenges such as initial investment costs, energy storage solutions, and policy implications are discussed, along with potential strategies to overcome these barriers. The findings emphasize the need for coordinated efforts among policymakers, industry stakeholders, and the public to promote sustainable charging solutions that can significantly reduce the carbon footprint of electric vehicles and contribute to a more sustainable energy future.

title: At the Crossroads of Compliance and Care: The Question of Power in Trauma-Informed Care Implementation in Child and Youth Residential Care
